description:
## Goal

The E.4 comparison harness (`18e69a1a`) showed aff3ct v4.4.0 decoding
~5-6x more frames/s than `gf2_coding::LdpcDecoder` on the CPU under
the committed run.sh invocations (DVB-T2: ~72-168 vs ~12-30 fps; NR:
~152-313 vs ~29-78 fps). The fps columns were informational and the
thread accounting was NOT normalized (our bin used 24 rayon workers;
aff3ct ran at its own threading default, never pinned). Establish the
true per-core gap, find out where the time goes, and recommend the
levers — measurements first, no speedup promises before profiling.

## Context

The project vision says 'push beyond existing implementations'. Our
GPU LDPC stage (639 fps decode-stage on gfx1030, `a930be7f` receipt)
already beats aff3ct's CPU by ~4-9x on the same host; the CPU scalar
decoder is the slow piece. The E.4 harness
(`dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/comparison/`) is the ready-made measurement
rig: `run.sh` hermetically builds aff3ct, `ldpc_bler_sweep` is the
gf2-sim arm, `export_alist` pins the bit-identical H.

## Deliverables

1. Pinned-thread apples-to-apples re-measure on the E.4 configs
   (DVB-T2 r1/2 N=64800 + NR BG1 Z=384 mother), quiet host:
   aff3ct `-t 1` vs single-rayon-worker `ldpc_bler_sweep`, and
   24-vs-24; per-core and per-host ratios documented.
2. Profile of the `LdpcDecoder` NMS decode hot path (perf record or
   equivalent): top contributors (memory layout, message storage,
   per-iteration allocation, Llr genericity) with numbers.
3. Evidence doc `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/cpu-decoder-profile.md`
   with the measurements, flamegraph/annotated summary, and a
   recommendation section ranking levers (e.g. compressed message
   layout, allocation hoisting, inter-frame AVX2 SIMD batch decode)
   by estimated ROI. Any follow-up implementation work is scoped
   from this doc, not before it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Pinned-thread measurements (1-vs-1 and 24-vs-24) for both
  E.4 configs on a verified-quiet host, committed in the evidence
  doc with exact invocations (reproducible).
- [hard] REQ-02: Profile identifies the top >=3 hot-path contributors with
  percentages; claims backed by profiler output, not inspection.
- [hard] REQ-03: Recommendation section ranks the candidate levers with
  measured or first-principles-estimated ROI; AVX-512/VNNI/GFNI
  work is explicitly OUT of scope here (routes to epic `7f809931`
  per project policy).
- [hard] REQ-04: `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- No decoder optimization implementation in this task (scoped by the
  evidence doc afterwards).
- No AVX-512 lane work (epic `7f809931`).
- No GPU kernel work (covered by study `43fb19e2`'s future epic).
title: Profile and close the CPU LDPC BP throughput gap vs aff3ct
